rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most important first step is to establish a clean, reliable baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest configuration in the space: it uses PCA (a deterministic, low-failure-risk encoder) on a single RNA profile with no image, aggregation, or fusion. This gives a well-defined reference accuracy for the RNA signal alone. From this baseline, I can then measure the marginal contribution of (a) better RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt), (b) multiprofile + aggregation, (c) the image modality, and (d) multimodal fusion. Starting with the simplest, most interpretable configuration reduces uncertainty about the floor performance and prevents conflating multiple design choices in the first experiment. Under a 10-experiment budget, anchoring to a simple baseline before exploring complexity is the most information-efficient use of experiment 1.

We have only one data point (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), so the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality carries useful signal at all. Testing config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) directly parallels the RNA baseline structure, isolating the image modality's standalone contribution. If image accuracy is substantially higher than 48.5%, it justifies investing remaining budget in multimodal fusion strategies; if it is comparable or lower, we should prioritize RNA encoder improvements (scvi, scgpt) and multiprofile aggregation instead. This single experiment most efficiently partitions the remaining 8-experiment budget between two very different search directions.

Evidence: RNA (pca_n2000, singleprofile) achieves 48.5% accuracy while image (resnet50, singleprofile) is very weak at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant signal source. The key uncertainty is whether the linear PCA representation is suboptimal and whether a learned nonlinear encoder (scvi_n200) can capture richer biological structure. This experiment (config_004: rna_only, singleprofile, scvi_n200) isolates the RNA encoder effect by changing only the encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while keeping model setting and profile setting identical to config_001. This is the best use of the next slot because: (1) improving the dominant modality is the highest-leverage move, (2) it provides a clean single-variable comparison to attribute any gain/loss to the encoder, (3) the result directly informs which RNA encoder to pair with multimodal fusion in later experiments, and (4) with 7 experiments remaining, establishing the best RNA backbone early maximizes the value of subsequent multimodal tests.

Evidence: scvi_n200 (0.5203 acc) clearly outperforms pca_n2000 (0.4849 acc) in singleprofile RNA-only settings, and image-only is very weak (0.2079). The multiprofile axis is entirely untested and is a critical structural choice that will inform all downstream multimodal experiments. This experiment tests whether multiprofile aggregation (avgpool, the simplest option) on top of the best-performing RNA encoder (scvi_n200) improves over the singleprofile baseline (config_004). It isolates the profile/aggregation effect with minimal added complexity. If multiprofile+avgpool helps, it validates exploring transformer aggregation and multimodal multiprofile configs; if it doesn't, we can focus remaining budget on encoder choice (scgpt) or multimodal fusion with singleprofile. This is the highest-information experiment for reducing uncertainty about a major design axis with 6 experiments still remaining.

Evidence: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieved 0.650 accuracy, a large jump over singleprofile scvi_n200 (0.520), confirming multiprofile+avgpool is the strongest design so far. Uncertainty: we have not tested whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool for multiprofile RNA. This experiment (config_006) isolates exactly that variable—changing only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding rna_encoder=scvi_n200 and multiprofile fixed. This is the best use of experiment 5 because it is a single-variable extension of our current best, directly informing whether we should use transformer aggregation in subsequent multimodal experiments (configs 020-021, 026-027, 032-033, etc.), and it reduces uncertainty about the aggregation design choice before committing remaining budget to more complex multimodal configurations.

The current best (config_006, rna_only/multiprofile/scvi_n200/transformer, acc=0.653) establishes that multiprofile + scvi_n200 is the strongest RNA configuration. However, scgpt encoder is completely untested in the multiprofile setting, and in single-profile it has not been compared to scvi_n200. Testing config_009 (scgpt, multiprofile, transformer) directly isolates the encoder effect against the current best by changing only the RNA encoder. This is critical because the encoder choice determines the base representation for any subsequent multimodal fusion experiments; with only 4 experiments remaining, I need to confirm whether scgpt could surpass scvi_n200 before committing budget to multimodal configs built on a potentially suboptimal encoder. If scgpt matches or beats scvi_n200, it opens a new promising branch; if not, I can confidently build multimodal experiments on the scvi_n200 base.

Evidence: The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653. RNA is clearly dominant over image (0.65 vs 0.21 image-only resnet50), and scvi_n200 + multiprofile is the strongest RNA configuration. The key unresolved question is whether multimodal fusion can add complementary signal beyond the 0.653 RNA-only ceiling. This experiment tests the most promising multimodal extension: scvi_n200 (best RNA encoder), multiprofile (biggest single boost observed), transformer aggregation (marginally best), and imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder than the weak resnet50, which scored only 0.21 standalone) with concat fusion. If this cannot beat 0.653, multimodal is likely not fruitful and remaining budget should focus on RNA-only refinements. If it does, we have a new best to build on. This is the best use of experiment 7 because it directly tests the highest-leverage unexplored direction (can a better image encoder + fusion surpass the RNA-only ceiling?) while keeping all other components at their empirically best settings, isolating the multimodal contribution.

The current best is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.721 accuracy, a strong jump over the best RNA-only (0.653). The evidence clearly shows: (1) scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder, (2) multiprofile is essential, (3) imagenet_vit_l is the strongest image encoder, and (4) multimodal fusion provides a substantial boost. The key remaining uncertainty within this winning configuration is the fusion method: concat (tested, 0.721) vs. weighted (untested). Config_039 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, isolating this single design choice. This is the cleanest and most informative next experiment: if weighted fusion improves accuracy, we gain a new best with 2 experiments left to confirm; if it does not, we confirm concat is optimal and can spend remaining budget on other refinements. With only 2 experiments remaining, this minimal-change comparison is the highest-value use of the next slot.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. All major design axes have been explored: multiprofile > singleprofile, scvi_n200 >> scgpt/pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l >> resnet50, weighted ≥ concat, and multimodal > RNA-only. The one remaining untested variation within the proven-best family is aggregation: in the RNA-only setting transformer (0.6530) marginally beat avgpool (0.6501), but in the multimodal setting the interaction between aggregation and fusion is untested. Config_037 changes only aggregation (transformer→avgpool) while keeping weighted fusion, multiprofile, scvi_n200, and imagenet_vit_l fixed. This isolates whether the transformer aggregation is truly necessary in the multimodal context or whether avgpool performs comparably. With only one experiment remaining after this, confirming (or ruling out) a small improvement in the best-known architecture is the highest-value use of the budget, as no other untested configuration combines all the individually-validated best components.

The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. Three of the four aggregation×fusion combinations for this top encoder pair have been tested (transformer+weighted=0.725, transformer+concat=0.721, avgpool+weighted=0.706). Config_036 (avgpool+concat) is the only missing cell in this 2×2 grid. Running it completes the interaction picture, confirming whether transformer+weighted is robustly superior or whether the small gaps (0.004 for fusion, 0.019 for aggregation) are within noise. Since this is the final experiment and no untested configuration is likely to surpass config_039 (scgpt and pca_n2000 were substantially weaker in RNA-only; resnet50 was far weaker than imagenet_vit_l), the best use of the last slot is to lock in a complete, interpretable characterization of the best-performing model family rather than test a configuration with very low prior probability of improvement.
